Inside the Danny Maude Swing Coach app, more than 700,000 golf swings show a common movement pattern that creates unnecessary effort, reduces clubhead speed and makes consistent ball striking more difficult.

The problem is that many golfers are trying to swing their body rather than swing the golf club.

Certain nutrient deficiency symptoms don’t always show up on a blood test. Learning to recognize these signs may be one of the best ways to identify and correct a deficiency.

Frequent yawning, hair shedding, and heavy legs are all common signs of iron deficiency, the most common nutrient deficiency in the world. Surprisingly, iron deficiency isn’t always caused by a lack of iron in your diet.

Hemoglobin is the protein in your blood that carries oxygen, and it needs iron to function properly. Ferritin represents your stored iron, which your body can use to maintain normal hemoglobin levels even when iron stores are low. An optimal ferritin level is around 70 to 100 ng/mL.

Iron deficiency can also be related to high insulin, gut inflammation, and fatty liver. A fatty liver can interfere with iron availability, making it harder for the rest of your body to access stored iron.

Other common causes of iron deficiency include:
• Low copper
• Low vitamin A
• Low stomach acid
• Menstruation
• Vegan diet
• High tea and coffee intake

videos.summary_source_text:
Ferrari 296 Speciale v Lambo Temerario DRAG RACE It’s time for an all-Italian showdown! 

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-1011

It’s time for an almighty Ferrari vs Lamborghini head-to-head! 

We’ve got our hands on the Lamborghini Temerario, and it’s lining up against the all-new Ferrari 296 Speciale! 

These are two of the most prominent and popular hybrid supercars to come out of Italy this year, and we’re about to see which will come out on top over the quarter-mile. So let’s take a look at the stats… 

Starting with the Lambo, it’s powered by a 4-litre twin-turbo V8, coupled with three electric motors. Together, they produce 920hp and 730Nm, with power sent to all four wheels via an 8-speed automatic gearbox. It’s the heavier of the two cars, at 1,790kg, and it has a starting price of £260,035. 

Then we come to the Ferrari. It’s ‘only’ packing a 3-litre twin-turbo V6, and it only has one electric motor. However, it still produces an incredible 880hp and 755Nm! It sends that power only to the rear wheels via an 8-speed automatic gearbox, but it’s a whole lot lighter than the Lambo at 1,510kg. As new, it costs £359,779. 

So how will this one play out - will the more powerful Lambo win it? Or will the weight difference prove decisive? There’s only one way to find out for sure… LET’S RACE!

videos.title: 27.11.26 - RIFT Training Day
videos.summary_source_text:
27.11.26 - RIFT Training Day RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Hindi - 27.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Computer scientist Scott Aaronson says he's virtually certain AI labs are sitting on bombshell discoveries, and that some of them will break the encryption protecting banks, messages and most of the internet. The same day, Google's AI posted six math papers, including a factoring proof that beats a record from 1992 on the exact math that encryption is built on. Google also published research on AI that keeps rewriting the code it runs in and remembers why each change worked, while DeepMind's agents now run experiments for the next Gemini on their own.

📩 Brand Deals & Partnerships: collabs@nouralabs.com
✉️ General Inquiries: airevolutionofficial@gmail.com

🔍 What You'll See
Scott Aaronson says he's "virtually certain" AI labs are sitting on algorithm bombshells, and that some "will break currently deployed cryptosystems."
SOURCE: https://scottaaronson.blog/?p=10379
A rumor that the labs can already split huge numbers fast spreads across X, and Aaronson asks people to stop citing him for it.
SOURCE: https://scottaaronson.blog/?p=10362
Google's Cogentic, a team of Gemini AI agents, posts six math papers in one day, including a factoring proof that beats a record from 1992.
SOURCE: https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/cogentic_research_papers
NIST plans to phase out RSA and elliptic curve encryption after 2030 and disallow them after 2035.
SOURCE: https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-nist-ir8547-pqc-transition-20261030-csa-st/
Google's Self-Improvement Memory paper shows an AI that rewrites its own harness scoring about 85 on office tasks with memory, versus 73 without it.
SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2611.18856
DeepMind's Koray Kavukcuoglu says AI agents now run experiments for the next Gemini model on their own.
SOURCE: https://the-decoder.com/ai-agents-now-control-part-of-deepminds-compute-for-gemini-experiments-but-recursive-self-improvement-remains-distant/

🚨 Why It Matters
Most of the internet's encryption rests on the bet that splitting huge numbers is too slow for any computer. The world's plan to replace it assumes the danger is quantum hardware, not an AI finding a shortcut on ordinary chips. And the same AI labs doing this math are teaching their systems to improve their own tools, which could speed up every discovery that comes next.

Florida has won three straight and has a point in seven of eight (6-1-1).

Sam Bennett scored with 23.2 seconds left by knocking in a Matthew Tkachuk shot; Florida trailed 2-1 with less than 5 minutes left before Eetu Luostarinen tied it off a pass from Brad Marchand. Aaron Ekblad also scored.

videos.title: 7 Reasons Your Body Tries to Regain Weight After Weight Loss | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
7 Reasons Your Body Tries to Regain Weight After Weight Loss | Dr. Mandell Have you ever wondered why losing weight can be so difficult, but gaining it back seems so easy? Your body has powerful biological survival mechanisms that can work against you after weight loss. Changes in hunger hormones, leptin, ghrelin, metabolic adaptation, energy expenditure, muscle mass, and your brain's appetite regulation can all contribute to weight regain. This is not simply about willpower or self-discipline — it's about understanding your physiology. In this video, I explain seven important reasons why your body tries to regain weight after weight loss and share practical, science-based strategies to help you manage hunger, preserve muscle mass, support your metabolism, improve satiety, and maintain a healthier weight. Understanding how your body responds to weight loss can empower you to make better nutritional and lifestyle choices for long-term success. Rather than constantly fighting your biology, learn how to work with it. Please share this video with someone who may benefit, and make it a great day! Dr. Alan Mandell

Lee Trevino Watches Back the Open He NEARLY Threw Away SUBSCRIBE -  https://bit.ly/RandaGolfSubscribe

Lee Trevino watches back his victory at the 100th Open Championship, 55 years on, as he relives his win at Royal Birkdale in 1971.

Fresh from winning the U.S. Open and the Canadian Open, Trevino arrived at Birkdale in the form of his life. He led by five with nine holes to play, before a double bogey on the 71st hole cut his advantage to a single stroke. He held on to beat Lu Liang-Huan, the much-loved "Mr Lu", by one shot. It was the first of Trevino's back-to-back Open titles.

videos.title: GPT-6 Astra vs Sol vs Terra — What Can $20 Actually Do?
videos.summary_source_text:
GPT-6 Astra vs Sol vs Terra — What Can $20 Actually Do? GPT-6 Astra vs GPT-6.1 Sol vs GPT-6.1 Terra — which AI model is actually worth using on the $20 ChatGPT Plus plan? The smartest model isn't necessarily the best choice. One delivers the highest reasoning performance, another comes surprisingly close at one-fifth the API price, and the third is significantly faster. But there's a catch: your ChatGPT Plus allowance isn't unlimited.

We put all three OpenAI models through four practical challenges inside ChatGPT Work using Sites: building an interactive finance dashboard, creating a 3D solar system, analyzing business data against a hidden answer key, and recreating a website from a screenshot.

Same environment. Same reasoning effort. Fresh conversations. One clean first attempt per model.

The goal? Find out whether GPT-6 Astra's extra intelligence actually translates into better results, whether Sol offers the best balance of performance and efficiency, and whether Terra's speed and visual reasoning make it the smarter everyday choice.

But the model comparison is only half the story.

**What does ChatGPT Plus actually give you for $20 per month?**

OpenAI's Plus subscription includes advanced GPT-6 reasoning, ChatGPT Work, Codex, Sites, expanded deep research, file analysis, and access to powerful AI tools. However, Astra, Sol, and Terra aren't all available in ordinary ChatGPT conversations on Plus.

Their availability depends on whether you're using Chat, Work, or Codex. And the differences matter.

We break down where these models actually live, how their usage limits work, and why choosing the wrong model could burn through your allowance faster than expected.

**GPT-6 Astra vs Sol vs Terra: The numbers**

According to Artificial Analysis, the three models score 57, 55, and 51 respectively on its intelligence index at maximum effort.

Meanwhile, Terra reaches approximately 72 tokens per second, compared with 49 for Sol and 41 for Astra.

API pricing reveals another major difference:

• GPT-6 Astra: $10 input / $50 output per million tokens

• GPT-6.1 Sol: $2 input / $10 output per million tokens

• GPT-6.1 Terra: $1 input / $5 output per million tokens

These are API prices, not additional charges for using the models within your Plus allowance. But they help explain why model selection matters.

We also examine reported creator demonstrations, including Blender 3D environments, browser games, Minecraft-style worlds, Microsoft Paint computer-control experiments, and interactive websites.

Some demonstrations are impressive. Others raise questions about reproducibility, human intervention, and whether they were actually completed on a standard Plus subscription.

Then there's the biggest limitation: usage caps.

OpenAI estimates roughly 5–45 Astra messages and 15–160 Sol messages within five-hour windows on Plus, depending on workload. Terra is designed to stretch allowances further, but exact limits aren't guaranteed.

We examine the restrictions around Work, Codex, Sites, agent mode, file uploads, and API billing — and compare the value proposition against Claude Pro and Google AI Pro.

**So is ChatGPT Plus worth $20 in 2026?**

That depends on whether you're a casual ChatGPT user, student, content creator, freelancer, small business owner, or developer.

More importantly, it depends on knowing when to use Astra for difficult reasoning, Sol for complex everyday projects, and Terra for faster visual or high-volume work.

Watch the full comparison to understand what you're actually paying for, where each model makes sense, and whether upgrading to ChatGPT Plus is the right decision.

Which model would YOU choose: Astra, Sol, or Terra? Let us know in the comments.

videos.title: Paul Maurice, Panthers Morning Skate at Washington Capitals
videos.summary_source_text:
Paul Maurice, Panthers Morning Skate at Washington Capitals Florida Panthers coach Paul Maurice speaks to the media before his team plays the host Washington Capitals on Nov. 28, 2026, at Capital One Arena. 

Florida is coming off a 5-3 win against the visiting Ottawa Senators.

Sasha Barkov and Brad Marchand were back in the lineup — with Marchand having a 3-point night, and Barkov scoring his first goal of the season. 

Florida has won two straight and pulled within 2 points of second in the Atlantic. 

Florida got goals from Barkov, Eetu Luostarinen, Niko Mikkola, Anton Lundell, and Sam Bennett in the win.

Jacob Markstrom made 25 saves. 

The Panthers next play host to the Lightning on Saturday.

Here's a look at the Downhill Skating System and how you can start skating more like the world's best players:

FREE TRAINING: https://train2point0.com/free-training

The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing, or "trying harder." Inspired by the movement signatures of Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, it teaches you to move with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles alongside efficient footwork and skating mechanics.

By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural momentum, you move faster with less effort.

Inside Train 2.0+ you'll learn to:
- Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
- Use direction changes that keep you deceptive and hold your optionality.
- Build NHL superstar mechanics, instead of repatterning the wrong movements.

videos.title: OpenAI Is Building the Next iPhone… Without a Screen?
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI Is Building the Next iPhone… Without a Screen? OpenAI spent $6.5 billion acquiring Jony Ive's hardware startup, io, and eighteen months later, the public still hasn't seen what that money bought. No official product photos, no confirmed specifications, no price, and no public name. And according to OpenAI's own court filings, the device won't ship before March 2027 at the earliest.

So what exactly are Sam Altman and the legendary designer behind Apple's iPhone building?

In this video, we investigate OpenAI's mysterious AI hardware project, separating confirmed facts from credible reports, patents, rumors, and speculation. Some of the most revealing information didn't come from an OpenAI announcement at all — it came from a trademark lawsuit involving audio startup iyO.

But what is the actual device?

Sam Altman has described it as a pocket-sized or desktop device that understands its surroundings — a "third device" alongside smartphones and laptops. Sworn court declarations confirm that the design was not finalized and that it was neither an in-ear nor a wearable device.

Reports suggest a screenless, voice-first AI assistant, but OpenAI has never officially confirmed the absence of a screen. Meanwhile, patents describing an expressive AI companion and a doughnut-shaped gadget have fueled speculation about its physical appearance. Neither patent has been confirmed as the actual product.

Then there's the release timeline.

In January 2026, OpenAI's Chris Lehane indicated that the first hardware device would be unveiled in the second half of 2026. However, subsequent court filings revealed that it would not ship to customers before the end of February 2027. As of late November 2026, no official unveiling has taken place.

But the distinction between an unveiling and a commercial release is important — and the timeline is more complicated than headlines suggest.

We also explore why OpenAI wants to enter the hardware business in the first place. ChatGPT currently operates within ecosystems controlled by Apple and Google. Dedicated AI hardware could give OpenAI greater control over voice interactions, background processing, contextual awareness, and the overall user experience.

The bigger ambition appears to be creating an entirely new interface for artificial intelligence.

Jony Ive's involvement makes this particularly interesting. The designer who helped create the iMac, iPod, iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch is now working on a product intended to reduce the stress and distractions associated with modern technology.

Altman wants an AI-first device that delivers peace and calm rather than the overwhelming experience of today's smartphones. But can good industrial design solve challenges involving privacy, battery life, connectivity, and AI reliability?

We examine three important pieces of evidence behind OpenAI's hardware ambitions:

• OpenAI and Broadcom's Jalapeño inference chip, reportedly delivering around nine times the throughput and twice the efficiency of existing chips.
• The reported 115,000-square-foot San Francisco office lease for OpenAI's hardware group.
• The Emotive Companion and doughnut-shaped device patents associated with Ive's team.

These developments demonstrate the scale of OpenAI's commitment, but they don't necessarily reveal what consumers will eventually receive. Jalapeño, for example, is a data-center chip, not a consumer hardware processor.

With Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses, Amazon Echo, and reported AI hardware projects from Apple and Google, the competition to define the next major computing interface is intensifying.

Yet OpenAI faces one fundamental problem: you already own a smartphone.

Why would consumers carry another device? Can it operate independently? How will it handle constantly sensing its surroundings? Will it require a subscription? And what can it actually do that a smartphone cannot?

OpenAI's hardware project could become the beginning of an AI-first computing era — or one of the most expensive lessons in consumer technology history.

The $6.5 billion investment is real. The engineering team is real. The ambition is real. But the product still needs to prove itself.

videos.title: Does Hang Time Predict Longevity?
videos.summary_source_text:
Does Hang Time Predict Longevity? Does grip strength predict longevity?

Researchers measured grip strength in more than half a million adults aged 40 to 69. Over the next seven years, people with a weaker grip were more likely to die. The test was simple. Squeeze a handheld device called a dynamometer as hard as you can. [1]

So why am I hanging from rings? Because I don’t have a dynamometer, but I can hang from rings or a bar anytime (and almost anywhere). I’m a big fan of an imperfect test I can do anytime. If I have to go to a lab or buy special equipment, how often am I actually going to test?

A dead hang tells me how long my grip can support my body weight. In one study, the best predictor of how long someone could hang from a bar was their grip strength relative to their body weight. [2]

Where did I get 90 seconds for men and 60 seconds for women? A study of 123 gym members used those exact times to classify a dead hang as “advanced.” The researchers chose those numbers based on experience testing people. I use them as fitness targets. Whether hitting either time tells you anything about your lifespan is still an open question. [3]

Q: How long can you hang?


REFERENCES

videos.title: Slår du för kort med drivern? Den bakre armen är lösningen…
videos.channel: Enklare & Bättre golf med Marcus Edblad PGA
videos.summary_source_text:
Slår du för kort med drivern? Den bakre armen är lösningen… Att verkligen sätta fart på drivern kräver att vi rätar ut den bakre armen väldigt tidigt och bestämt. Denna video guidar dig i både tanke och utförande.

#golf #golftips #golfswing 

0:00 Intro - Sträck ut tidigt för att slå längre med drivern. 
1:00 Att förstå hur slaget påverkas är nyckeln till framgång. 
3:00 En enkel övning för känsla och förståelse. 

Nu finns det möjlighet att genom appen Skillest göra mig till din personliga tränare. Du hittar mig på denna länk: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

Låt mig hjälpa dig finna bättre slag, bollträff, riktning och svinghastighet. Oavsett om du slår en wedge, järnklubba eller driver kan du med dina händer lära dig golfslag som du inte trodde var möjliga. Längre och rakare slag kräver alltid träning men något alla kan lära sig.  

Vare sig du kämpar med en slice eller en hook så har jag videos som kan guida till bättre golf. Är du nybörjare så kan du börja med min grönt kort eller nybörjarkurs.

Försök ersätta dåliga vanor med nya bättre vanor. Oavsett vilket loft eller skaft din klubba har så är det du som bestämmer vad som ska hända. Oavsett om det står callaway, ping, titleist eller taylor made på klubban så kan du slå bra slag.

Var noga med vad du tittar på. Det finns många duktiga instruktörer på nätet, några av mina favoriter är Mike Malaska, Mike Dunaway, Mike Austin.

Försök fokusera på grunderna i slaget bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår. Träna med fördel på en sak i taget. Tränar du din svinghastighet måste du tillåta att det går snett och tränar du raka slag kan du inte samtidigt svinga i max fart.

Ha tålamod och låt det ta sin tid, luras inte av genvägar som bara gör att du tappar fokus från det viktiga. Golf kommer alltid vara svårt men vi kan med träning se till att vi blir bättre för varje dag som går.

Titta mycket på golf på TV. Bryson Dechambeu, Dustin Johnson, Rory Mcilroy kan inspirera till längre slag och andra som Tiger Woods, Viktor Hovland, Ludvig Åberg och Phil Mickelson kan ge dig fantasi att skapa nya slag.

Träna styrketräning för hela kroppen för att må bra genom livet och skapa en effektiv maskin. Träna händer, handleder och armar för att skapa en effektiv release och mer svinghastighet.

Du kan finna inspiration i filmer som Happy Gilmore, Tin Cup eller Bagger Vance. Filmer som Rocky kan ge dig motivation att ta dig till gymet. Legender som Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sylvester Stallone eller Hulk Hogan kan få dig att vilja bli starkare och Moe Norman, Arnold Palmer, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead eller Jack Nicklaus kan inspirera dig att bli en bättre golfare. 

Ge aldrig upp i sökandet och träningen för att få bästa bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår.

Round 2 Highlights | 2027 BMW Australian PGA Championship Highlights from the second round at the season opener of the DP World Tour 2027 season, the BMW Australian PGA Championship at The Lakes in Sydney. Featuring Adam Scott, Min Woo Lee, Alex Noren and more!

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

The 2027 DP World Tour season gets under way with the Opening Swing - four events across three countries and two continents it is the first of five Global Swings on the 2027 DP World Tour global schedule. The schedule comprises three distinct phases, beginning with the Global Swings followed by the Back 9, with the season then culminating with the DP World Tour Play-Offs in November. The first shot of the season will once again be hit in Australia as the BMW Australian PGA Championship moves south from Brisbane to Sydney and The Lakes Golf Club. The BMW Australian PGA Championship brings a host of local stars home with former winners Min Woo Lee, Adam Scott and Cam Smith all in action. Ryder Cup star Alex Noren - a 12-time winner on the DP World Tour is also playing as is David Puig who defends his title. As well as four prestigious trophies and valuable Race to Dubai and Ryder Cup points, there is plenty to play for on the Opening Swing. The player who earns the most Race to Dubai points across the five events will be crowned Opening Swing champion and earn entry into all events in Phase Two of the season.

videos.title: 26.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
26.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Hindi - 26.11.26 - RIFT Update with Lucky
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 26.11.26 - RIFT Update with Lucky RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

Following another devastating defeat, the Cowboys owner and general manager admits Dallas suffered a major setback and says the entire organization must be evaluated after another game slipped away.

Jones addresses the controversial late-game decision to go for it instead of punting, the missed field goal, special teams mistakes, and the Cowboys' inability to finish games.

But the biggest question: Will Jerry Jones make a coaching change during the Cowboys' upcoming 11-day break?

Jerry also discusses Brian Schottenheimer's future, Dak Prescott's performance, Joe Milton's big game for Philadelphia, and why the Cowboys have struggled to build momentum this season. videos.title: Puffy Eyes? Try This on One Side—Then Compare | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Puffy Eyes? Try This on One Side—Then Compare | Dr. Mandell Wake up with puffy eyes or under-eye bags? In this video, I demonstrate a gentle facial drainage massage you can try on just one side first, then compare both sides. You’ll learn where to use light, rhythmic pressure near the collarbone and around the ear, followed by a soft glide beneath the eye along the orbital bone and down the side of the face and neck. Use a feather-light touch—never press on the eyeball or dig into the delicate under-eye tissue. If fluid retention is contributing to puffiness, many people may notice a significant change.  Stop if anything hurts. Sudden, painful, persistent swelling or changes in vision should be assessed by a healthcare professional. Try the technique with me, compare one side with the other, and tell me what you notice. Please share this video with your friends and family. Wishing you and your family many blessings! ❤️🙏 Dr. M

videos.title: Claude Just Solved the Biggest Problem in Mathematics (SuperIntelligence Is Here)
videos.summary_source_text:
Claude Just Solved the Biggest Problem in Mathematics (SuperIntelligence Is Here) Did Claude just help solve the Riemann Hypothesis, one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics? A staggering 17,374,215 lines of Lean code across 175,187 files have already survived multiple independent machine checks.

On November 20, 2026, Levent Alpöge, a number theorist working at Anthropic, published an announcement claiming that he and Claude had produced a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis — a mathematical problem that has remained unsolved for 167 years and carries a $1 million Millennium Prize.

The Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative have publicly expressed full confidence in the correctness of the formal proof.

But Anthropic hasn't officially announced a solution. The Clay Mathematics Institute still lists the problem as unsolved as of November 23. And mathematicians are still working to understand why the proof actually works.

This could represent one of the most significant breakthroughs in AI-assisted mathematical research.

The story began in August 2026, when Anthropic revealed that an unreleased research version of Claude had attempted to solve the Riemann Hypothesis. According to Anthropic, the experiment involved approximately:

• 650 candidate mathematical ideas
• 60 coordinated AI subagents
• 31 million output tokens
• Thousands of shell commands
• Dozens of mathematical research papers

Claude failed to solve the complete hypothesis during that experiment. However, it reportedly discovered a new unconditional theorem that increased the proportion of simple zeros on the critical line to 67.2%, a substantial improvement over the previous record of approximately 41.7%.

That earlier breakthrough laid the groundwork for what came next.

Claude reportedly contributed substantive mathematical ideas, including a specific chain of theta lifts. Alpöge even described Claude as far outpacing him during the later stages of the project.

But without publicly available interaction logs, it remains impossible to independently determine exactly how much of the discovery came from Claude and how much came from human mathematical expertise. The specific Claude model used for the November proof also remains undisclosed.

Michael Rubinstein at the University of Waterloo successfully compiled all 175,187 modules with zero failures. Approximately 61.6 GB of exported proof data was subsequently checked using nanoda, an independent Lean kernel written in Rust, which verified 1,484,729 declarations without finding errors.

Andrew Sutherland at MIT conducted a separate audit. Additional independent proof checkers, including con-leche and con-ron, also accepted the formal proof.

The theorem matches Mathlib's pre-existing definition of the Riemann Hypothesis. There are no hidden assumptions of the hypothesis itself, no unfinished proof gaps using Lean's "sorry" keyword, and no substitution of an easier mathematical problem.

Mathematicians can mechanically verify the proof, yet they are still attempting to reconstruct its underlying mathematical reasoning. Robin Zhang, Michael Rubinstein, James Maynard, Kevin Buzzard and other experts feature in the developing discussion surrounding this extraordinary result.

We also examine Alessandro Masullo's separate 900-page claimed proof, The Music of the Primes, which appeared during the same week but has not received comparable independent formal verification.

How does Claude's achievement compare with Google DeepMind's AlphaGeometry, AlphaProof and Gemini Deep Think? What separates solving International Mathematical Olympiad problems from discovering genuinely new mathematics? And could combining large language models with formal proof assistants like Lean fundamentally change scientific discovery?

We also explain why proving the Riemann Hypothesis would not immediately break RSA or elliptic-curve encryption, why nobody has received the $1 million Millennium Prize yet, and what the Clay Mathematics Institute requires before officially recognizing a solution.

The biggest story might not simply be whether Claude helped solve the Riemann Hypothesis. It might be that AI-assisted mathematical discovery has reached a point where formal verification can arrive before human comprehension.

Warsofsky On The Hot Seat? + The Future of the Canucks? w/ David Quadrelli | Daily Faceoff Live The Buffalo Sabres, Anaheim Ducks and Utah Mammoth all picked up big wins Wednesday night, but are the Sabres actually better than we think? We break down Buffalo’s recent play and ask whether this team is truly a contender or simply… average. Plus, the San Jose Sharks get blown out as questions start to mount around Ryan Warsofsky.

Cale Makar returned to the Colorado Avalanche lineup and immediately made an impact, picking up two points as the Avs shut out the Montreal Canadiens. Meanwhile, Montreal falls to 0-2 since acquiring Dylan Larkin, and we look at what’s gone wrong for the Canadiens’ top line and whether their Stanley Cup hopes are already starting to take a hit.

We also break down some of the biggest moments from around the NHL, including a wild night for Joonas Korpisalo, a questionable play from Andrei Vasilevskiy, and a potential Fight of the Year candidate.

Plus, David Quadrelli of DFO Vancouver joins us to discuss the Canucks’ culture under Manny Malhotra, which veterans could be sold, and what Filip Hronek’s future could mean for Vancouver’s trade return.

SURDEGSBRÖD - recept alla lyckas med Enkelt surdegsbröd - steg för steg, utan maskin.

*RECEPT - SURDEGSBRÖD*
200 g surdegsgrund
350 g vatten
500 g vetemjöl (hög proteinhalt att föredra)
25 g vatten + 13 g salt

*VANLIGA FRÅGOR OM SURDEGSBRÖD*

*Hur gör man en surdeg från start?*
Blanda lika delar mjöl och vatten i en burk och låt stå i rumstemperatur. Mata med nytt mjöl och vatten varje dag. Efter ungefär 5-7 dagar bubblar den och doftar syrligt, och då går den att baka med.

*Vad är skillnaden mellan surdeg och levain?*
Levain är det franska ordet för surdeg. I Sverige används det oftast om vetesurdeg och om ljusa bröd bakade på den.

*Hur matar man surdegen, och hur ofta?*
Enklaste är att röra ner lika delar mjöl och vatten. I rumstemperatur behöver den matas varje dag, i kylen räcker ungefär en gång varannan vecka. Mata den 10 - 12 timmar innan du bakar så att den är på topp, alltså har ungefär dubblat sin volym.

*Kan man använda köpt surdeg?*
Flytande surdeg från butiken är oftast gjord för att ge smak tillsammans med jäst och orkar inte jäsa brödet själv. Till det här receptet behövs en levande surdegsgrund. Gör en egen eller be om en klick från en vän eller ett bageri.

*Råg eller vete i surdegen?*
Båda fungerar. Råg kommer igång lättast, vete ger en mildare smak.

*Vad är autolys, och varför viker man degen?*
Autolys betyder att mjöl och vatten får vila innan saltet tillsätts. Då tar mjölet upp vattnet och glutenet börjar utvecklas av sig självt. Vikningarna under jäsningen ger degen styrka utan att du behöver knåda.

*Behöver man jäskorg?*
Nej. En bakform som i videon eller en skål med en väl mjölad kökshandduk fungerar lika bra.

*Måste man baka i gryta?*
Nej, men grytan håller kvar ångan och ger bättre resning och skorpa. Utan gryta: grädda på en riktigt varm plåt eller baksten och kasta in en deciliter vatten på en plåt i botten så luften inte blir för torr.

*Hur kalljäser man över natten?*
Ställ det formade brödet i kylen i 8-16 timmar och grädda det direkt från kylen. Det ger mer smak och gör brödet lättare att snitta.

*Hur snittar man brödet?*
Med ett rakblad eller en riktigt vass kniv, ett snabbt och bestämt snitt strax innan brödet ska in i ugnen.

*När är brödet klart?*
När innertemperaturen är ungefär 98 grader. Låt det svalna på galler till under 60 grader innan du skär i det.

*Varför jäser eller bubblar inte surdegen?*
Oftast står den för kallt. Den trivs bäst vid 24-28 grader. Ha tålamod och fortsätt mata, det är vanligt att den stannar av några dagar i början.

*Varför luktar surdegen aceton?*
Den är hungrig. Mata den så försvinner lukten. Vätska på ytan är också ofarligt, rör ner den eller häll av. Mögel är däremot luddigt och färgat, och då ska surdegen slängas.

*Hur förvarar man surdegen?*
I kylen med locket löst påskruvat. Ska du inte baka på länge går den att frysa eller torka.

*Hur förvarar man brödet, och går det att frysa?*
Med snittytan mot skärbrädan eller i en papperspåse håller det 3-4 dagar. Skiva och frys det du inte hinner äta.

*Är surdegsbröd nyttigt?*
Den långa jäsningen bryter ner fytinsyra, vilket gör att kroppen lättare tar upp mineralerna i mjölet. Många tycker också att det är lättare för magen. Hur nyttigt brödet är beror annars mest på vilket mjöl du använder.

*Innehåller surdegsbröd gluten?*
Ja. Surdegsbröd på vete eller råg innehåller gluten.

I kylen med locket löst påskruvat. Ska du inte baka på länge går den att frysa eller torka.

*Hur förvarar man brödet, och går det att frysa?*
Med snittytan mot skärbrädan eller i en papperspåse håller det 3-4 dagar. Skiva och frys det du inte hinner äta.

*Är surdegsbröd nyttigt?*
Den långa jäsningen bryter ner fytinsyra, vilket gör att kroppen lättare tar upp mineralerna i mjölet. Många tycker också att det är lättare för magen. Hur nyttigt brödet är beror annars mest på vilket mjöl du använder.

*Innehåller surdegsbröd gluten?*
Ja. Surdegsbröd på vete eller råg innehåller gluten.

videos.title: Grok 4.8 Is Coming… Elon Musk 2.5 Trillion Massive Upgrade!
videos.summary_source_text:
Grok 4.8 Is Coming… Elon Musk 2.5 Trillion Massive Upgrade! Elon Musk says Grok 4.8 has 2.5 trillion parameters, a completely rebuilt software stack, and roughly 19% more parameters than Grok 4.7. But when asked how it compares to Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, his response was surprisingly direct: "Not as good."

Even more interestingly, Musk believes Grok 5 could surpass Opus 5.5 within two to three months. So what exactly is xAI trying to achieve with Grok 4.8?

As of November 25, 2026, xAI has not officially launched Grok 4.8 for general use. There are no independent benchmarks, official API listings, confirmed pricing, or firm release dates. Almost everything we know about the upcoming AI model comes directly from Elon Musk's posts on X.

In this video, we separate Musk's claims from confirmed information, examine the Grok 4.8 development timeline, and investigate where xAI actually stands in the increasingly competitive AI race.

According to Musk, Grok 4.8 has completed pre-training, entered reinforcement learning, and undergone limited testing through Grok Bot. He has also revealed that several different model variants are currently in beta, potentially pointing toward multiple versions optimized for different workloads.

But the biggest development might not be the parameter count.

Musk claims xAI abandoned Google's JAX and the SGLang inference framework, rebuilding its entire reinforcement learning and inference stack from scratch using C/C++, with help from Starlink engineers. This could potentially improve hardware efficiency, inference speed, and operating costs. However, xAI has yet to publish measurements demonstrating those improvements.

We also explain why 2.5 trillion parameters doesn't automatically translate into superior intelligence, how dense and mixture-of-experts architectures differ, and why active parameter counts could matter more than the headline number.

Grok 4.7 provides an important reference point. Despite a reported 40% increase in parameters over Grok 4.6, it launched with an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 46, behind Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 at 53. We examine its coding benchmarks, CursorBench 4.0 results, Terminal-Bench 4.0 discrepancies, and GDPval performance to understand what this previous launch could tell us about Grok 4.8.

Meanwhile, the competition hasn't stopped.

During Grok 4.8's extended development cycle, Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.2, OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, and Google launched Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Neon.

The reported Artificial Analysis scores for GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2 have reached 62 and 65, respectively, although changes to benchmark methodology complicate direct comparisons. Grok 4.8 is entering a significantly more competitive market than the one xAI faced when development began.

But intelligence benchmarks aren't the only way xAI could win.

Grok 4.7 launched at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens, substantially undercutting several frontier AI models. If Grok 4.8 can maintain competitive pricing while delivering faster inference, improved token efficiency, and reliable autonomous agent capabilities, it could offer meaningful advantages for developers and businesses.

Musk has also teased a "lightning-fast" Grok 4.8 variant designed to handle simpler requests through Grok Bot. Could xAI be preparing a family of models focused on speed, affordability, and long-running AI agents rather than simply chasing the highest benchmark scores?

Then there's the possibility that Grok 4.8 is laying the technological foundation for Grok 5 rather than attempting to defeat the current frontier models itself.

We investigate the unanswered questions surrounding Grok 4.8's architecture, context window, API availability, pricing, release date, coding performance, and real-world capabilities. We also examine whether Musk's projected Grok 5 timeline is realistic given xAI's history of delayed releases.

Is Grok 4.8 worth waiting for? Can xAI close the widening gap with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google? Or is the company's biggest AI breakthrough still another generation away?

Glöggmarinerad fläskfilé med Saint Agur-sås, klyftpotatis, brysselkål och morötter
Ingredienser (4 port)

KÖTTET
600 g fläskfilé
Rapsolja (till att bryna köttet)
Svartpeppar, salt

GLÖGGMARINAD
1 dl glögg
½ dl neutral olja
3 msk soja
2 msk riven ingefära
1 msk chiliflakes
Svartpeppar
1 tsk salt

UGNSROSTADE ROTFRUKTER
12 potatisar, gärna Asparges, delade på längden
200 g brysselkål, halverad
4 morötter, i stavar
3 schalottenlökar, i klyftor
6 vitlöksklyftor, skalade
½ dl olivolja
30 g smör
Salt och svartpeppar

SAINT AGUR-SÅS
20 g smör
1½ msk vetemjöl
2 dl fond
1 dl mjölk
3 dl grädde
100 g Saint Agur
1 msk japansk soja
Svartpeppar
Salt (smaka av först)

GÖR SÅ HÄR:

videos.title: Does Sauna Make You Live Longer?
videos.summary_source_text:
Does Sauna Make You Live Longer? Does sauna increase your lifespan? Maybe… 

A Finish study followed 2.3K middle-aged men for 20 years, and those who used a sauna four to seven times a week had a roughly 40% lower risk of dying during the study than men who used it once a week. 

So what might explain it?

1. Your heart works harder. Your heart rate goes up and more blood flows to your skin to cool you down. That’s where the comparison to low-intensity cardio comes from.  

2. Heat shock proteins may play a role. Heat can trigger these proteins, which help protect your cells under stress. Whether that helps people live longer is still an open question.  

3. Sweating out toxins? This is real, but limited - and the evidence is thin

TAKEAWAY? For most of us, 4x+/week sauna is a great “someday” plan. But today, strength, stretch, and cardio are top of the todo list as always.

videos.title: Nope, Pilates doesn’t target stabilizer muscles
videos.summary_source_text:
Nope, Pilates doesn’t target stabilizer muscles Joe Pilates himself didn’t explain the anatomy and biomechanics of “why” the practice works, so it’s no surprise there are lots of pop health myths floating around. 

But today, with so much research in exercise physiology and millions of people practicing, I think it makes sense to talk about the real benefits.

It’s not cardio. 
It’s not muscle hypertrophy training. 
It doesn’t magically target smaller or deeper muscles while ignoring big ones. 
It’s not a spiritual practice (unless you’ve decided it is). 

The reformer is a horizontal, spring-loaded cable machine. It lets you move through a full range of motion with low impact, train muscular coordination, build core strength (uniquely), and improve joint health.

That’s a LOT! 

Sure, you can strap a rowing machine to one end or jump around and do HIIT just like you can go running with dumbbells in your hands. But rather than try to make it everything, I think it makes more sense to leverage its inherent strengths. videos.summary_source_text:
I Specced the Most Expensive Aston Martin Meet the most powerful front-engined Aston Martin EVER! 

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-2611

Meet the Aston Martin Valen! 

It’s an all-new, V12-powered limited-run Aston, and Mat’s about to find out if it’s one of the coolest Aston Martins ever created. 

Not only will he get to take a look around the exterior and interior, but he’ll also have a chance to spec his own Valen! But before that, let’s look at the standard spec, starting with the exterior…

On first impressions, the Valen is a seriously aggressive piece of kit! The front end is dominated by a huge, aggressive grille that stretches across the length of the car. There’s also a huge front splitter, a vent in the creased bonnet to help with airflow, and thin headlights that sit either side of the iconic S-curve in the front intake. Along the side, there are massive carbon-fibre side sills, and around the back, the most notable feature is the four exhaust outlets. There’s a floating-designed full-length light bar, a massive diffuser, and the rear tyres are exposed. It looks incredible! 

On the inside, there are several similarities to the Vanquish, although it’s different enough to ensure you don’t get the two mistaken. A number of physical switches have been removed, and the centre console is now covered in a 3D-printed metal lattice structure. There’s a rotary switch to control the infotainment screen, and there’s a huge number of options to choose from to make the Valen your own, such as several seat options. 

The Valen is powered by a 5.2-litre twin-turbo V12, and it produces an incredible 850hp and 1,000Nm. This power is sent to the rear wheels via an 8-speed automatic gearbox, and it can hit 60mph in just 3 seconds. It also has a huge top speed of 214mph! 

The Valen has a starting price of £1,500,000, and it’s limited to just 150 units. But do you think it’s the coolest car Aston Martin has ever produced? Let us know in the comments! Meet the most powerful front-engined Aston Martin EVER!

videos.title: 25.11.26 Ep.26 (Part 9) - The Prop Execution Checklist
videos.summary_source_text:
25.11.26 Ep.26 (Part 9) - The Prop Execution Checklist Understanding how markets operate is only part of becoming a disciplined trader. The next step is understanding how much it actually costs to execute a trade – and, more importantly, how much of your potential profit remains after all those costs have been taken into account.

In this session, we build on our understanding of Central Limit Order Books (CLOBs), Automated Market Makers (AMMs), liquidity pools, market depth and execution discipline. We introduce a more comprehensive pre-trade checklist before moving into the mathematics of trading costs, separating the visible expenses from the less obvious costs that can quietly erode profitability.

A strategy may look profitable on a chart or in a backtest, but its true performance can be very different once execution costs are included. Professional trading is not simply about identifying opportunities. It is about preserving capital, managing execution and ensuring that the gross trading edge translates into a positive net result.

Topics Covered

The Expanded Pre-Trade Checklist – Assessing the market structure, liquidity model, visible depth, pool reserves, concentrated liquidity, expected costs, slippage tolerance and urgency before entering a trade.

Understanding the Trading Venue – Identifying whether you are trading through a Centralised Finance (CeFi) or Decentralised Finance (DeFi) environment, and whether the market uses an order book or an AMM.

Entry and Exit Liquidity – Why traders must consider whether sufficient liquidity will still be available when they need to close their position.

Planning for Failure – Preparing for unfilled limit orders, failed transactions, disappearing liquidity, price gaps and pools becoming too thin to support an exit.

Headline Fees vs All-In Execution Costs – Why the venue with the lowest advertised fee is not necessarily the cheapest once spread, slippage and market impact are included.

Capital Preservation – Why protecting trading capital must remain a constant priority, particularly when trading with funding provided by a prop trading firm.

From Price Trader to Market Structure Trader – Moving beyond headline prices to understand the actual liquidity, depth and execution conditions behind a market.

Gross Performance vs Net Performance – Why a strategy's apparent returns can be significantly reduced once the real costs of trading are deducted.

The Net Trading Result Equation – Understanding how gross trading results are reduced by explicit and implicit execution costs.

Explicit Trading Costs – Broker commissions, exchange fees, trading fees, clearing fees, swap fees, network costs and platform charges.

The Compounding Effect of Small Fees – How seemingly insignificant percentages and basis-point charges can accumulate into substantial costs over repeated trades.

Protocol and Swap Fees – Understanding how fees differ between platforms and liquidity pools, including examples involving Uniswap.

Bid-Ask Spread – How buying at the ask and selling at the bid creates an immediate execution cost, and why traders effectively pay for immediacy.

Slippage – The difference between the expected execution price and the final average fill, including the possibility of positive price improvement.

The One-Tick Problem – How a small difference in execution can become a substantial financial cost when trading multiple contracts repeatedly.

Market Impact – How large orders consume available liquidity, move prices and potentially influence the behaviour of other market participants.

Information Leakage – Why institutional traders must consider how their trading intentions can become visible to the market.

Funding Costs in Perpetual Futures – How periodic funding payments between long and short positions can affect the profitability of trades held over time.

Blockchain Network Costs – Understanding gas fees, network congestion and why failed on-chain transactions can still consume fees without completing the intended trade.

Opportunity Cost – The financial consequence of missing a trade because a limit order was never filled.

Market Orders vs Limit Orders – Comparing execution certainty with price control, and understanding the different risks associated with each order type.

What You Will Learn

By the end of this session, you should understand why trading performance must be measured after execution costs, not simply by looking at entry signals, win rates or gross returns.

We also introduce the concept of implementation shortfall – the gap between the trading decision you intended to make and the result you actually achieved. This important topic will be continued in the next session.

videos.title: It's simple. Better distance and impact with early extension of the trail arm…
videos.channel: Easier & Better golf with your guide Marcus Edblad
videos.summary_source_text:
It's simple. Better distance and impact with early extension of the trail arm… Don’t be one of the 90% that slice your driver. The early extension of the trail arm is the only fix you need. Start doing the drill in the video and you will soon hit your driver a lot longer and better.

#golfswing #golf #golftips #swingspeed 

Online lesson are now a possibility on Skillest: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

0:00 Intro -Why do I speed train with an iron?
1:00 Extend with good timing
4:00 The strike will give you the answers you need. 

Let me help you get an effortless golfswing with speed, distance and accuracy. I call it the circle of speed. A good release will help you to a better impact and longer drives and irons without slice and hook. How to swing a golf club need to be adjusted to your skill level and experience. 

Long and straight is the goal for everyone but it takes time. Try to focus on one thing not everything when you practise. Impact, face control and swingpath will always be the most important part to drill. We focus too much on rotation but no good golf shot will be executed just by rotating. 

We also need to understand that many myths in golf are missleading. Everything that you find on the internet isn’t true. Ben Hogan, Sam Snead are two of the legends that are often misunderstood.  To understand golf we need to take it step by step and learn every part of the swing before we move on to the next. It's like a big jigsaw puzzle that we all can figure out. 

I will never call a slice sexy but a high draw is beautiful in a very special way. Some pro's that hit draw: Rory McIroy, Xander Schauffele, Patrick Reed, Sepp Straka, Bryson Dechambeau  and many, many more. 

We shall not keep our head still, only start with the hips, look only at the ball or keep the left or right arm straight. Understand what do do with the club and let your body find the best way possible. 

This is not Rick Shiels, Saguto golf, Danny Maude, Meandmygolf, the Average Golfer, Malaska, Mark Crossfield, Alex Elliot Golf or Paige Spiranac. This is a method that anyone can learn if you give it a chance. 

If you use callaway, ping, titleist, takomo or taylor made clubs doesn’t matter you can learn to hit good golf shots. Your loft or your shaft on the club will not change but you can always get better. 

Find what inspires you. Golf basics are the same for everyone. The pga tour, longdrivers or other good golfers can all help you find better golf shots. Watch what they do instead of listed to what they say. Listen mostly to your body and figure out what you need to do to produce the same results as the pros on TV. Be careful when you watch a golf swing in slow motion. The result isn't always what the golfer is trying to do. Feel and real are seldom the same. 

We can find inspiration in a lot of things. You can find training motivation watching movies like Rocky, Tin Cup or Happy Gilmore and find mental inspiration in legends like Arnold Schwarzenegger, Hulk Hogan, Sylvester Stallone or Mike Tyson. Maybe we sometimes need to hear about crazy achievements from people like David Goggins, Jocko Willink, Ct Fletcher, Jim Rohn or Tony Robbins. 

Mike Malaska, Mike Austin, Mike Dunaway, Pete Cowen and Steve Pratt are some of my favorite golf instructors online. Find the tips that make your golf better. Decide what you want to hit. I teach a draw but many like a fade and nobody likes a hook or slice. 

Your hips or your lag is not the key to golf. Your hands will decide the shot and you can do like Tiger Woods and trust your hands. Teach your hands to hit different shots. Hit big hooks and slices to understand what happens. Only straight is not gonna teach you anything. 

Bryson Dechambeu and Kyle Birkshire can inspire you to hit it longer. Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson can give you inspiration and motivation to test new things and new golf shots. Linn Grant, Viktor Hovland and Ludvig Aberg can show you the future of golf. 

The Masters, Players Championship, The Players, The Open and US Open can make you love golf even more. See the best in the world solve all the problems we all need to master any golf course. Golf is a craft and you need fantasy, feel and skills to master it.

Questions my videos will answer:

How to swing faster. How to hit longer. How to swing faster. How to hit your irons better. How to be better at anything. How to master the circle of speed. How to get a better short game. How to hit your wedge better. How to release the golf club. How to rotate in golf. Best tips for beginner golfers. How to hit down on the ball. How to hit up on the ball. How to rotate hips in the golf swing. How to hit straight every time. How to stop slicing. How to swing effortlessly. 

#subscribe #golftips #pga  #hurricane 


Filmed with Iphone 15 pro or Iphone 18 Don’t be one of the 90% that slice your driver. The early extension of the trail arm is the only fix you need. Start doing the drill in the video and you will soon hit your driver a lot longer and better.

#golfswing #golf #golftips #swingspeed 

Online lesson are now a possibility on Skillest: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

0:00 Intro -Why do I speed train with an iron?
1:00 Extend with good timing
4:00 The strike will give you the answers you need. 

Let me help you get an effortless golfswing with speed, distance and accuracy. I call it the circle of speed. A good release will help you to a better impact and longer drives and irons without slice and hook. How to swing a golf club need to be adjusted to your skill level and experience. 

Long and straight is the goal for everyone but it takes time. Try to focus on one thing not everything when you practise. Impact, face control and swingpath will always be the most important part to drill. We focus too much on rotation but no good golf shot will be executed just by rotating. 

We also need to understand that many myths in golf are missleading. Everything that you find on the internet isn’t true. Ben Hogan, Sam Snead are two of the legends that are often misunderstood.  To understand golf we need to take it step by step and learn every part of the swing before we move on to the next. It's like a big jigsaw puzzle that we all can figure out. 

I will never call a slice sexy but a high draw is beautiful in a very special way. Some pro's that hit draw: Rory McIroy, Xander Schauffele, Patrick Reed, Sepp Straka, Bryson Dechambeau  and many, many more. 

We shall not keep our head still, only start with the hips, look only at the ball or keep the left or right arm straight. Understand what do do with the club and let your body find the best way possible. 

This is not Rick Shiels, Saguto golf, Danny Maude, Meandmygolf, the Average Golfer, Malaska, Mark Crossfield, Alex Elliot Golf or Paige Spiranac. This is a method that anyone can learn if you give it a chance. 

If you use callaway, ping, titleist, takomo or taylor made clubs doesn’t matter you can learn to hit good golf shots. Your loft or your shaft on the club will not change but you can always get better. 

Find what inspires you. Golf basics are the same for everyone. The pga tour, longdrivers or other good golfers can all help you find better golf shots. Watch what they do instead of listed to what they say. Listen mostly to your body and figure out what you need to do to produce the same results as the pros on TV. Be careful when you watch a golf swing in slow motion. The result isn't always what the golfer is trying to do. Feel and real are seldom the same. 

We can find inspiration in a lot of things. You can find training motivation watching movies like Rocky, Tin Cup or Happy Gilmore and find mental inspiration in legends like Arnold Schwarzenegger, Hulk Hogan, Sylvester Stallone or Mike Tyson. Maybe we sometimes need to hear about crazy achievements from people like David Goggins, Jocko Willink, Ct Fletcher, Jim Rohn or Tony Robbins. 

Mike Malaska, Mike Austin, Mike Dunaway, Pete Cowen and Steve Pratt are some of my favorite golf instructors online. Find the tips that make your golf better. Decide what you want to hit. I teach a draw but many like a fade and nobody likes a hook or slice. 

Your hips or your lag is not the key to golf. Your hands will decide the shot and you can do like Tiger Woods and trust your hands. Teach your hands to hit different shots. Hit big hooks and slices to understand what happens. Only straight is not gonna teach you anything. 

Bryson Dechambeu and Kyle Birkshire can inspire you to hit it longer. Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson can give you inspiration and motivation to test new things and new golf shots. Linn Grant, Viktor Hovland and Ludvig Aberg can show you the future of golf. 

The Masters, Players Championship, The Players, The Open and US Open can make you love golf even more. See the best in the world solve all the problems we all need to master any golf course. Golf is a craft and you need fantasy, feel and skills to master it.

Questions my videos will answer:

How to swing faster. How to hit longer. How to swing faster. How to hit your irons better. How to be better at anything. How to master the circle of speed. How to get a better short game. How to hit your wedge better. How to release the golf club. How to rotate in golf. Best tips for beginner golfers. How to hit down on the ball. How to hit up on the ball. How to rotate hips in the golf swing. How to hit straight every time. How to stop slicing. How to swing effortlessly.

Avalanche SHUTOUT Canadiens 6-0 in Heated Matchup | Avs Postgame Breakdown | 11.25.2026 The Colorado Avalanche delivered a statement performance at Ball Arena, shutting out the Montreal Canadiens 6-0.

Mark Robinson breaks down Colorado's dominant win, including an impressive showing from the Avs' power play, Devon Toews' two-goal performance and Mackenzie Blackwood's 27-save shutout.
