videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 25.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Why Powerful People Always Get Away With It While We Suffer | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Why Powerful People Always Get Away With It While We Suffer | Dr. Mandell When people with power put their own interests first, the effects can reach far beyond them. The decisions made by leaders and influential people can shape the lives of families, workers, and entire communities—especially when the people affected have little say in what happens. This video is a reminder that power comes with responsibility. Leadership should mean listening, acting with integrity, and considering who may be hurt by a decision—not simply asking who stands to benefit. When the consequences fall on ordinary people, accountability matters. We should pay attention to the choices being made, ask who benefits, and remember who may be left carrying the cost. Because when the powerful put themselves first, someone else may pay the price. What do you think real leadership should look like?

videos.title: Falk om DIF-krisen och Kimbys framtid: ”Då är du ju körd”
videos.summary_source_text:
Falk om DIF-krisen och Kimbys framtid: ”Då är du ju körd” Fyra raka förluster, 4–15 i målskillnad och en alltmer pressad Robert Kimby.

Vad händer egentligen bakom stängda dörrar när ett lag hamnar i en förlustspiral? När börjar spelarna ifrågasätta varandra – och när riktas blickarna mot tränaren?

Nichlas Falk och Henrik Sjöberg analyserar krisen i Djurgården i veckans DIF News.

Så lyssnar du på Hockeynews PLUS-poddar

Direkt på Hockeynews: Lyssna i spelaren högst upp i artikeln.

Spotify: Sök upp podden, välj ett avsnitt med hänglås och koppla ditt Hockeynews PLUS-konto.

Apple Podcasts: Gå till hockeynews.consume.sesamy.com/sv, logga in med PLUS och välj podd. Klicka på “Klicka här för att lyssna”, välj Apple Podcasts och tryck “Följ”.
Har du inte Hockeynews PLUS kan du teckna ett abonnemang. Du behöver bara koppla kontot en gång. Därefter får du nya avsnitt direkt i din poddapp.

Ur innehållet:
►  Betyg 1–10 på ALLA nio nyförvärv.
►  De dyra felträffarna i Wikegårds och Due-Bojes lagbygge.
►  Krisens olika faser i omklädningsrummet.
►  Wikegårds prestige i satsningen på Kimby.
►  Spelidén som inte fungerar – så måste DIF förändras.

videos.title: Anthropic Just Raised $1.5 Trillion — But Something Strange Is Happening
videos.summary_source_text:
Anthropic Just Raised $1.5 Trillion — But Something Strange Is Happening Anthropic just pulled off the biggest IPO in history, closing a $119.5 billion transaction and reaching a valuation near $1.5 trillion. But behind the record-breaking debut is a much more complicated story: roughly $117 billion in expected net proceeds, nearly $895 billion in disclosed purchase and lease commitments, unusual Wall Street restrictions, and a stock that lost about 20% of its opening value in just two trading sessions.

So did Anthropic just win the AI funding race against OpenAI, or did it create one of the most expensive bets in technology history?

The numbers are extraordinary. Anthropic went from $41 million in revenue in 2023 to $4.585 billion in 2025, then reported $33.242 billion in just the first nine months of 2026. Its private valuation climbed from $61.5 billion in March 2025 to $965 billion in May 2026, before its November IPO pushed the fully diluted valuation toward $1.5 trillion.

And this wasn't a conventional IPO.

Then came another $26 billion from seven strategic investors: Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Microsoft, Broadcom, Micron, and TSMC.

Google and NVIDIA alone contributed $20 billion. But many of these investors are also Anthropic's suppliers, infrastructure partners, or competitors. That raises an important question about AI's increasingly interconnected financing ecosystem: when technology companies invest billions in the customers buying their computing infrastructure, where does strategic investment end and circular financing begin?

The IPO's market debut added another twist.

Anthropic shares, trading under ANT, opened at $111.50 on November 19, approximately 34% above their $83 offering price. The stock briefly touched $115, implying a valuation approaching $2 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

By November 20, shares had fallen to $88.91.

Meanwhile, Reuters reported that Anthropic imposed unusually strict conditions on some of the 22 banks managing the offering. According to people familiar with the process, certain teams were limited to four bankers, sensitive documents were watermarked, and some bankers faced six-month restrictions on working with competitors including OpenAI, Cursor, DeepSeek, and Hugging Face.

The reported internal name? Project Lantern.

But the biggest revelation comes from Anthropic's SEC filings.

Despite generating positive operating cash flow during the first nine months of 2026, Anthropic disclosed $451.2 billion in future payments for leases that had not yet commenced, plus $105.7 billion in additional commitments after September 30. Another disclosure places purchase commitments and leases near $895 billion.

These obligations are spread across years, not immediately payable debt. Still, they reveal the scale of Anthropic's bet on AI infrastructure.

And there are other complications: approximately $18.8 billion in compute expenses, pricing discounts that reduced third-quarter revenue by roughly $600 million, copyright litigation, government-related risks, and a governance structure that leaves public shareholders with limited voting power.

Then there's OpenAI.

Sam Altman's company reportedly raised $122 billion at an $852 billion valuation in March 2026 and claims more than 1.2 billion weekly ChatGPT users. Anthropic, meanwhile, is pushing deeper into enterprise AI with Claude Code, Claude Fable 5.2, Mythos 5.2, financial-services agents, and AI-powered scientific research.

Anthropic has now become a publicly traded frontier AI lab while OpenAI remains private. That means investors can scrutinize Anthropic's financial performance, infrastructure spending, and profitability every quarter.

We break down how the IPO reached $119.5 billion, where the money actually goes, why the seven strategic investors matter, what Reuters uncovered about the deal, and why Anthropic's enormous infrastructure commitments may be more consequential than its record valuation.

The financing victory is undeniable. Whether Anthropic can turn that capital into sustainable profits is an entirely different question.

videos.title: Paul Maurice: Barkov, Marchand Return to Florida Panthers v Senators
videos.summary_source_text:
Paul Maurice: Barkov, Marchand Return to Florida Panthers v Senators Florida Panthers coach Paul Maurice speaks to the media before his team plays host to the Ottawa Senators on Nov. 25, 2026.

Maurice said Sasha Barkov and Brad Marchand will be back in the lineup.

Both practiced with their likely lines — and the Panthers have now waived two players to get Barkov off LTIR and into the lineup.

Florida is coming off a 4-3 win against the Buffalo Sabres.

Sam Bennett had his second hat trick of the season with Sandis Vilmanis getting the game-winner late in the third. 

The line of Bennett, Vilmanis, and Eetu Luostarinen had all four goals and three assists. 

Jacob Markstrom made 17 saves. 

The Panthers play the Sens on Wednesday then travel to Washington on Friday afternoon.

videos.title: Gemini 5 Is Coming: Google’s 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade!
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 5 Is Coming: Google’s 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade! Google Gemini 5 could be much more than another powerful AI model. Google is already developing artificial intelligence that can operate computers, generate entire interactive worlds, control humanoid robots, coordinate autonomous agents, and solve previously unanswered scientific problems. And these technologies are beginning to work together.

The most fascinating clues about what Gemini 5 could become are hidden inside Google's existing AI ecosystem. From Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon to Genie 4, Gemini Robotics 2, Deep Think, and Antigravity, Google appears to be building something far more ambitious than a chatbot.

In this video, we investigate Google's bigger AI strategy, the potential architecture of Gemini 5, and how Google DeepMind could fundamentally change the way humans interact with artificial intelligence.

Gemini 4 Argon already features a one-million-token context window and a maximum output length of one million tokens. According to Google, Argon helped develop a memory-safe video decoder that runs 2.7 times faster than the existing Rust implementation, contributed to restructuring six million lines of Chromium code, and exceeded a published quantum computing optimization baseline by 40%.

But intelligence alone won't determine who wins the AI race.

We examine how Google competes against OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2, including intelligence benchmarks, inference costs, business automation, and Google's enormous infrastructure advantage through its TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max accelerators.

Then there's Google's increasingly sophisticated approach to autonomous AI agents. Project Mariner's technology has moved into Google's broader ecosystem, while Gemini Swarm and Orchestrator demonstrate how specialized AI models can collaborate. Carbon handles complex reasoning and planning, while Hydrogen focuses on faster, more affordable execution.

Instead of building one model that does everything, could Google be building an entire team of AI models?

We also explore Genie 4, DeepMind's interactive world model capable of generating explorable environments with native real-time audio. Combined with Gemini Omni and advanced reasoning models, world simulation could eventually become an important tool for AI planning, decision-making, and robotics training.

Gemini Robotics 2 takes that possibility into the physical world. Using Apptronik's Apollo humanoid robot, Google demonstrated whole-body coordination and AI-assisted robotic movement. In one experiment, Argon helped develop a solution that reportedly enabled a humanoid robot to complete seven consecutive successful cornhole shots, compressing weeks of simulation work into hours.

Google's scientific AI research is equally fascinating. From Gemini Deep Think achieving gold-medal-level performance at the International Mathematical Olympiad to Aletheia solving open Erdős problems, AlphaFold transforming protein research, and AlphaEvolve discovering improved algorithms, Google is exploring AI systems that generate, evaluate, and refine their own solutions.

What happens when all these capabilities begin to converge?

Gemini 5 could represent a shift from conversational AI toward coordinated intelligence capable of understanding objectives, developing plans, performing extended tasks, simulating potential outcomes, and verifying its own work.

However, these are not officially confirmed Gemini 5 features. This video separates Google's documented research and company-reported achievements from informed predictions about its next-generation AI systems.

We also examine the major obstacles standing between Google's AGI ambitions and reality, including autonomous agent reliability, prompt injection, world model consistency, robotic limitations, computational efficiency, and human oversight.

The next major AI breakthrough might not be a chatbot that gives better answers. It could be an intelligent system that you delegate entire objectives to.

And if Gemini 5 becomes a significant step toward that future, the biggest question won't simply be how intelligent it is. It will be how much responsibility we're willing to give it.

videos.title: Testosterone side effects (they don't tell you)
videos.summary_source_text:
Testosterone side effects (they don't tell you) I’m not (yet) on TRT, and here’s why…

I’ve still got my hair, and I’m hoping to hang on to it for a few more years. My sleep is pretty bad now, and I don’t want it to get worse (although I know it might improve). Mostly, I don’t want to start a medication I’d likely have to take for the rest of my life.

That’s easy for me to say because, thanks to genetics and lifestyle, my levels are fine for now. But I’m not naive. I’m fairly certain there’ll come a time in the near future when I’ll change my mind. I’m just strategically stalling for now.

My personal belief is that everyone should get to age however they want. Age naturally, use hormones, whatever suits you.

So why this post? I know dozens of men on TRT, and almost none of them were properly informed about the potential side effects.

Worse still, men are starting TRT at younger and younger ages, many in their 30s and even their 20s.

Note: I’m a random fitness guy on the internet, and this is not medical advice. My male clients are all middle-aged or older, and they’re getting bombarded with messages about peptides and hormones all day long. They’re confused. We all want to look and feel younger, so it’s a mind-bender.

Fat shots, thin shots and hitting behind the ball usually come down to a low point that's too far back, when you want the club traveling down to hit the ball first and the ground second. In Eric Cogorno's experience, higher handicap golfers who struggle with this have one of two main issues: hips that don't get forward enough in the golf downswing, or a club that gets under the swing plane. The fix starts with a golf drill that gets your belt buckle forward of the ball and over your left ankle by impact, with about 45 degrees of hip rotation and roughly 70 to 80 percent of your weight on your left foot, the same hips-forward move Eric shows in the swings of Scottie Scheffler, Tommy Fleetwood and Collin Morikawa. Add a takeaway and delivery with the club on plane down your toe line, and you have the two keys Eric uses to control your low point so you can stop hitting behind the ball and strike it solid any time the ball is on the ground. If you leave this video without trying the feel of pushing off the inside of your right foot, you're leaving solid, ball-first contact on the table.

What You'll Learn:
• How to stop hitting behind the ball
• How to hit irons ball first, then the ground
• How to get your hips forward in the golf downswing
• How to blend hip rotation with moving your hips forward
• Why your weight should be on your left foot at impact
• Why getting under the swing plane moves your low point back
• How to control your takeaway for solid contact
• High handicap golf tips for fat and thin shots

Metformin depletes vitamin B12, and the most common form of vitamin B12 may not correct the problem.

Vitamin B12 is essential for building the myelin sheath that protects your nerves, supporting red blood cell production, and maintaining healthy cognitive function, focus, mood, and memory.

Metformin interferes with vitamin B12 absorption and transport and can affect the liver’s ability to recycle B12 properly.

Metformin also reduces glucose production in the liver and carries a boxed warning for lactic acidosis. Vitamin B1, particularly in the form of benfotiamine, may help reduce the risk of lactic acidosis.

Most vitamin B12 supplements contains cyanocobalamin, a cheap synthetic form of B12. Hydroxocobalamin is a much better option. 

Taking 1000 to 2000 mcg of hydroxocobalamin can help improve B12 levels when digestive problems interfere with absorption. Magnesium glycinate, at 300 to 400 mg daily, can also help support vitamin B12 function.

videos.title: 24.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
24.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Is this bold move the missing piece for a Canadiens’ Stanley Cup run, or did Detroit Red Wings score big by stockpiling picks and prospects? Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson debate the merits of the deal, comparing it to past Avalanche trades—including the controversial Mikko Rantanen move—and question whether Colorado’s front office got fair value for their stars.

Spotlight shifts to Montreal’s visit to Ball Arena, with special focus on how Larkin might impact the Canadiens’ offensive chemistry against a resilient Avalanche squad. videos.title: Hindi - 24.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 24.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Drink Okra Water Every Day — What Happens to Your Body | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Drink Okra Water Every Day — What Happens to Your Body | Dr. Mandell What happens when you soak okra in water overnight? In this video, I take a closer look at okra’s slippery, gel-like mucilage, made largely of complex carbohydrates, and explain why its texture has caught the attention of researchers. Viscous soluble fibers can hold water and thicken digestive contents. That added viscosity may slow how quickly food leaves the stomach and how rapidly carbohydrates are digested and absorbed, helping explain why fiber-rich foods can support a more gradual rise in blood sugar after a meal. In the large intestine, gut bacteria ferment some fibers into short-chain fatty acids, including butyrate, which is used by cells lining the colon. Fiber also helps retain moisture and add bulk to stool, supporting regularity. Researchers have studied okra preparations in people with elevated blood sugar, and reviews of clinical trials have reported improvements in measures such as fasting glucose, A1c, and cholesterol. Okra’s soluble fiber is also being investigated for how it interacts with bile acids, which play a role in fat digestion and cholesterol metabolism. I’ll show you how to make okra water with fresh pods and explain why you may also want to enjoy the whole vegetable—steamed, roasted, or added to soups—to get its fiber and other nutrients. Okra is a simple, versatile vegetable with fascinating properties and an easy place in a balanced eating pattern. Have you tried okra water? Share your experience in the comments!

Selected PubMed Research:

- Therapeutic potential of okra (Abelmoschus esculentus) in dysglycaemia and metabolic dysfunction: A systematic review and meta-analysis across the diabetes spectrum. Experimental Physiology, 2026. PMID: 41823653. pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov

- Xie Y, et al. Effects of soluble fiber supplementation on glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Clinical Nutrition, 2021. PMID: 33162192. pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov

- Mechanisms underlying the cholesterol-lowering properties of soluble dietary fibre polysaccharides. PMID: 21776465.

videos.title: Brady Tkachuk Ready to Face Ottawa Senators with Panthers for Second Time
videos.summary_source_text:
Brady Tkachuk Ready to Face Ottawa Senators with Panthers for Second Time Florida Panthers forward Brady Tkachuk speaks to the media after his team held a practice in Fort Lauderdale on Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026. 

Tkachuk will face the Ottawa Senators, where he spent the first eight seasons of his career, for the second time with the Panthers on Wednesday.

After practice, coach Paul Maurice had an update on the potential return of Sasha Barkov and Brad Marchand — likely on Wednesday against the Senators.

Both practiced with their likely lines — and the Panthers have now waived two players to get Barkov off LTIR and into the lineup.

Florida is coming off a 4-3 win against the Buffalo Sabres.

Sam Bennett had his second hat trick of the season with Sandis Vilmanis getting the game-winner late in the third. 

The line of Bennett, Vilmanis, and Eetu Luostarinen had all four goals and three assists. 

Jacob Markstrom made 17 saves. 

The Panthers are off until hosting the Senators on Wednesday.

videos.title: Grok 5 Explained: Elon Musk's Biggest AI Gamble — Everything We Know
videos.summary_source_text:
Grok 5 Explained: Elon Musk's Biggest AI Gamble — Everything We Know Elon Musk says Grok 5 will be a massive 6-trillion-parameter AI model, twice the size he claims Grok 3 and Grok 4 were built on. But more than a year after that announcement, xAI still hasn't released Grok 5, published a single benchmark, or officially confirmed its architecture.

Meanwhile, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google have all released new flagship AI models. The competition is getting stronger, and Grok 5's release timeline keeps moving.

So what is actually happening behind the scenes at xAI? How powerful could Grok 5 really be, and can it compete against GPT-6.2 Astra, Claude Fable 5.2, Mythos 5.2, and Gemini 4 Neon?

In this video, we break down everything we know about Grok 5 as of November 2026, separating officially confirmed information from Elon Musk's statements, speculation, and misleading claims surrounding the upcoming AI model.

We examine the significance of Grok 5's proposed six trillion parameters, the difference between total and active parameters in mixture-of-experts architectures, and why a larger AI model doesn't necessarily translate into greater intelligence.

Musk has also described Grok 5 as inherently multimodal, with real-time video understanding, audio processing, improved tool use, and tool creation capabilities. But there is an important distinction between native multimodal intelligence and a language model accessing separate specialist models.

Then there's the Grok 5 release date. After missing multiple target windows, Musk's latest comments suggest a potential January or February 2027 launch. However, that remains an inference rather than an officially confirmed release date. Grok 4.8 and Grok 4.9 have also been mentioned as intermediate steps on xAI's roadmap.

While Grok 5 remains unreleased, xAI has been building an increasingly sophisticated AI ecosystem:

• Grok 4.20 and its multi-agent reasoning architecture
• Grok 4.5, Grok 4.6, and Grok 4.7
• Grok Build and autonomous agentic coding
• Grok Bot and persistent cloud computers
• Grok Image 2.0 and Video 1.5
• Grok Voice 3.0
• Long-horizon reinforcement learning and self-verification

We also investigate xAI's enormous Colossus supercomputer infrastructure, including NVIDIA H100, H200, GB200, and GB300 GPUs, Spectrum-X networking, and the company's claim of more than one million H100-equivalents.

But does that mean Grok 5 is being trained on one million physical GPUs? Not necessarily. The distinction between compute equivalents, physical hardware, and actual training allocation matters far more than the headlines suggest.

We examine independent Artificial Analysis benchmarks for Grok 4.7, including its Coding Agent Index score of 56, DeepSWE performance of 73%, Terminal-Bench 4.0 improvements, professional reasoning capabilities, inference speed, and substantial output-token consumption.

Grok 4.7 offers a 500,000-token context window and API pricing starting at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens. But cheaper token pricing doesn't automatically mean cheaper completed tasks.

We compare xAI's position against OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, and Google's Gemini 4 Neon, while examining the potential strategic advantages of SpaceX's acquisition of xAI, real-time X data, and massive computing infrastructure.

We also explore the safety controversies, prompt-injection risks, legal challenges, environmental concerns, and infrastructure constraints that could complicate Grok 5's launch.

Ultimately, the biggest question isn't whether Grok 5 will have six trillion parameters. It's whether xAI can turn its enormous infrastructure, autonomous agents, reinforcement learning, and multimodal technology into a genuine capability leap that independent testing can verify.

Could Grok 5 become the world's leading AI model? Could it deliver meaningful progress toward AGI? Or will it arrive as another expensive frontier model competing in an increasingly crowded market?

12:59 What Independent Testing Says About Grok 4.7
15:06 The Rivals Grok 5 Has to Beat

18:13 What Would Make Grok 5 Actually Matter

videos.title: Please Fix These 10 Exercises Now (I'M BEGGING YOU!)
videos.summary_source_text:
Please Fix These 10 Exercises Now (I'M BEGGING YOU!) Fix Your Exercise Mistakes Here - https://athleanx.com
Subscribe to this channel here - http://bit.ly/2b0coMWd

You might be doing these 10 gym exercises wrong, even if you’ve had them in your workout for years. In this video, I’m going to show you the most common form mistakes I see and how to fix each one. Some put unnecessary stress on a joint or tendon. Others are harder to spot because the weight keeps moving even after the muscle you’re trying to build has stopped doing much of the work.

First up is the preacher curl. Look at where your shoulders are in relation to your elbows. If you sit low behind the preacher bench and reach your arms out over the pad, you put your biceps tendon in a tough position at the bottom of the curl. Sit up taller, lean over the bench, and drive your elbows down into the pad. You’ll feel your lats engage and give you better leverage while your biceps do the work of curling the weight.

Next is the Bulgarian split squat. Ever put your back foot on the bench and hopped around trying to find the right spot for your front foot? Start by sitting on the bench and extending your working leg in front of you. Plant that heel, stand up, and you’ve found your distance. I’ll show you how to position your back foot so more of it stays in contact with the bench. Now your front leg can do the work.

On crunch pulldowns, watch the distance between your ribs and your pelvis. If you sit your hips back toward your heels, you can move the rope a long way while doing very little with your abs. Imagine there’s a wall right behind your butt that you can’t push back into. Keep your hips there and bring your ribs toward your pelvis. That rounding of your spine is what you want your abs to produce on every rep.

For lat pulldowns, one of my favorite fixes is to swap the long lat bar for a short triceps pushdown bar. The shorter attachment takes the guesswork out of how wide to place your hands. A narrower grip lets your elbows get out in front of you for a stretch at the top. From there, drive your elbows down close to your sides as you pull.

Even if you can knock out plenty of pushups, check where your elbows are at the bottom of the rep. Start face down on the floor with your arms overhead. Slide your elbows down until they’re about 45 degrees from your sides, then set your hands so your elbows stack over your wrists. Now pay attention to your feet. Rock forward on your toes as you lower your chest and back as you press the floor away. That small shift lets you press through an arc much like you would on a bench press.

If balance is the first thing to go on lunges, look at where your feet land. Even a long stride can leave you wobbling if your feet land on the same narrow line. Step out a little wider to give yourself a bigger base of support. Whether you’re doing forward lunges or reverse lunges, a slight turn of your torso to square up with the working leg can help you feel more stable.

On cable crossovers, watch your shoulder as your hand crosses your chest. If the shoulder rolls forward and your chest chases your hand, you’re missing the contraction you wanted in the first place. Keep your chest up as your arm comes across. Think about moving your chest back as your hand goes forward. Try pulling from high to low and feel how hard you can squeeze your pec at the finish.

The lying triceps extension is easy to get wrong at the top. If you straighten your elbows with the weights directly over your chest, gravity does very little to challenge your triceps in that position. Keep your upper arms angled slightly back toward your head as you extend your elbows. You’ll feel the difference at the top without having to add weight.

For facepulls, use a long rope or attach two ropes so you have room to get your hands back alongside your head. An overhand grip makes it easy to pull with your elbows and leave your hands out front. Grab the rope from underneath and lead with your hands. Think of finishing in a double biceps pose to get the external rotation you want at the shoulder.

Last up is the cable lateral raise. Run the cable in front of your body and step away from the machine so your working arm can reach across you. Let the cable draw that arm into a stretch before you raise it out to the side. If you stand too close to the stack and start with your arm at your hip, you miss the part of the rep that makes the cable such a good option for your side delts.

videos.title: Geely utvecklar bilar till halva priset – vad händer då med Volvo i Sverige?
videos.summary_source_text:
Geely utvecklar bilar till halva priset – vad händer då med Volvo i Sverige? Läs reportaget: https://alriksbilar.se/artiklar/geely-volvo-utveckling/

Kommer Volvo att utveckla nya bilar i Sverige om 5–10 år? Jag har varit på plats hos Geelys enorma utvecklingscentrum utanför Shanghai, där 8 000 ingenjörer tar fram nyckelfärdiga bilar åt vem som helst – till halva kostnaden och på halva tiden. Tolv biltillverkare är redan kunder och över 100 bilprojekt pågår samtidigt.

Vad betyder det för Volvo i Göteborg? Hade EX90:s mjukvaruproblem och EX60:s förseningar hänt om bilarna utvecklats i Kina? Och vad återstår av europeisk bilindustri när all teknik går att köpa färdig? Jag fick inte filma där det var mest intressant – så jag berättar vad jag såg.

videos.title: Jensen Huang’s $1 Trillion Revenge!!
videos.summary_source_text:
Jensen Huang’s $1 Trillion Revenge!! Nvidia stock surged 31.48% in a single trading session, adding roughly $952 billion in market value after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO. Just eleven days earlier, he had resigned amid a growing controversy involving an admitted affair, alleged foreign intelligence links, and mounting national security concerns.

Even more remarkably, Nvidia's board had explicitly stated six days earlier that it did not intend to reinstate Huang. Then it unanimously reversed its decision.

So what actually happened behind closed doors?

In this video, we break down the extraordinary eleven-day crisis that shook Nvidia, Wall Street, Washington, and the entire artificial intelligence industry.

We examine how Jensen Huang's admitted extramarital affair with Singapore-based businesswoman Alice Huang escalated into a national security controversy, involving reported suspicions of Chinese intelligence connections, congressional scrutiny, and a criminal investigation into Megaspeed, a company that purchased Nvidia chips.

But there is a critical distinction between confirmed facts, reported allegations, and speculation. Beijing has denied the espionage claims, and Nvidia's independent investigation remains ongoing.

We also explore what happened to Nvidia without Jensen Huang. Colette Kress stepped in as interim CEO, Harvey Jones became the company's first-ever board chair, and Nvidia began searching for a permanent replacement. Despite reporting record quarterly revenue of approximately $116 billion, Nvidia saw more than a trillion dollars in market value disappear during the leadership crisis, amid a broader AI market sell-off.

Then came the pressure to bring him back.

Elon Musk publicly supported the "Stand with Jensen" petition, which reportedly attracted more than 190,000 signatures. Major investors reportedly contacted Nvidia's board. And President Donald Trump claimed he personally convinced board members to reinstate Huang.

Nvidia's official announcement acknowledged receiving input from senior levels of the United States government, but it left several important questions unanswered.

Who provided that input? What national security assurances were given? And how much did Nvidia's collapsing stock price influence the board's decision?

We analyze the differences between Nvidia's original resignation announcement and its reinstatement statement, the political pressure surrounding the reversal, and why Huang's return triggered one of the most extraordinary stock market rallies in Nvidia's history.

However, the nearly trillion-dollar comeback requires context. The Nasdaq rose 6.5%, the S&P 500 gained 4.7%, and AI infrastructure companies such as CoreWeave also experienced significant gains. Not all of Nvidia's recovery can be attributed to Huang's return.

Then there's the catch: reinstatement does not mean exoneration.

Nvidia's independent investigation remains open. Questions surrounding semiconductor export controls, alleged chip smuggling, Megaspeed, Chinese access to advanced AI chips, and Nvidia's compliance practices remain unresolved.

With Jensen Huang scheduled to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3 at a hearing titled "Protecting America's AI Advantage," the controversy is far from over.

We also examine the bigger implications for corporate governance, America's semiconductor leadership, the AI infrastructure market, and the growing concentration of power within the technology industry.

Perhaps the most uncomfortable lesson from these eleven days is the extent of Nvidia's key-person risk. Investors are not simply betting on Nvidia's GPUs, software ecosystem, or record-breaking revenue. They are also betting on Jensen Huang himself.

What happens when the stability of the world's AI infrastructure depends so heavily on one individual?

And did Nvidia's board reverse its decision because of new evidence, political influence, financial pressure, or a combination of all three?

CHAPTERS

videos.title: Unboxing IFRS 18 – Management-defined Performance Measures (MPM)
videos.summary_source_text:
Unboxing IFRS 18 – Management-defined Performance Measures (MPM) Vilka av era egna resultatmått kommer att behöva upplysas om i noterna – och vad krävs egentligen för att uppfylla de nya kraven? 

Sedan IFRS 18 publicerades har management-defined performance measures, så kallade MPM:s, varit ett av de mest omdiskuterade områdena i den nya standarden. I korthet innebär kraven att vissa av de resultatmått som företag använder i sin externa kommunikation, mått som "justerat rörelseresultat" eller "justerad EBITDA", nu ska upplysas om i en not i den finansiella rapporten och därmed bli föremål för revision. Men vilka mått uppfyller egentligen definitionen av ett MPM? Hur förhåller sig MPM till ESMAs riktlinjer om alternativa nyckeltal (APM)? Vilka upplysningar och avstämningar behöver vara på plats och vad gäller för delårsrapporter? 

I det här avsnittet djupdyker vi i just dessa frågor tillsammans med Lisa Sagström och Daniela Casadei, redovisningsspecialister på PwC. Tillsammans med moderator Mian Heldesten, rådgivare inom finansiell rapportering, går vi igenom definitionen av MPM, de praktiska gränsdragningarna och vad bolag bör göra redan nu. 

Detta är det femte avsnittet i vår LinkedIn Live-serie Unboxing IFRS 18, där vi löpande gör kortare nedslag i den nya standarden tillsammans med olika gäster som delar sina perspektiv och praktiska erfarenheter. IFRS 18 ersätter IAS 1 och ska tillämpas för räkenskapsår som börjar 1 januari 2027 eller senare, inklusive jämförelseinformation. Från det här avsnittet får du med dig konkreta insikter som du kan ta med dig direkt in i ert IFRS 18-arbete.

videos.title: 3 Reasons NOT to Lift Heavy
videos.summary_source_text:
3 Reasons NOT to Lift Heavy I’m sick of fitness influencers mocking light weights as if heavy lifting is the only way to go.

Heavy lifting is great. But it’s not for everyone, not for every body, and not for every stage of fitness.

So much of the fitness industry runs on the same pitch. You’re not doing enough. You’re not strong enough. You’re not aging right.

But here’s a little secret. You get to decide what you want from exercise. And here are three legitimate reasons to give yourself full permission to skip the heavy weights right now.

You don’t like it

If it stresses you out, if it’s uncomfortable, or if you don’t like the way it makes your body look or feel, don’t do it.

You can’t do 6 push-ups

For years, I didn’t use weights at all. Push-ups and pull-ups were already “heavy” for me.

You’re new to strength training (or coming back after a break).

Your tendons take time to adapt to heavier loads, and as you get older, it makes sense to give yourself that time. Start with a weight you can control and build up over the weeks. A serious joint injury can derail your training for months. Taking a few extra weeks to work up to heavier weights is a trade I’ll take.

For most of my adult life, I trained with my own body weight and got great results (for my lifestyle fitness goals). Now, as I approach 50, I’ve added 75 minutes of dumbbell work a week. It’s made a big difference. I can measure it in how much more I can lift, and I can see and feel it in my body.

But who knows what I’ll feel like 5, 10, or 20 years from now? Maybe I’ll go back to bodyweight only training.

So if pink weights are your thing right now, I’m cool with that. Invite me over and we can do a session together. I’m sick of fitness influencers mocking light weights as if heavy lifting is the only way to go.

videos.summary_source_text:
The Last 60 Minutes Of The Final Round | 2026 DP World Tour Championship Last 60 Minutes Of The Final Round of the 2026 DP World Tour Championship

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

After visiting 25 countries across five continents, the DP World Tour’s schedule reaches a climax this week in Dubai, for the DP World Tour Championship, marking the final event of the 2026 Race to Dubai season. Since 2009, the DP World Tour Championship has annually played host to the season-ending event. Contested over 72 holes, with no cut, the final Rolex Series event features a $10 million prize fund, the biggest of the 2026 Race to Dubai season. 50 players have made their way to the second of back-to-back Rolex Series events, which form the DP World Tour Play-offs. There are two key pieces of silverware on offer this week, The DP World Tour Championship and the Harry Vardon Trophy. The battle for the Race to Dubai title comes to an end this week at Jumeirah Golf Club as players vie to end the year as DP World Tour Number One. There are still nine players in the running to end the year at the top of the Ranking. Eugenio Chacarra, the only three time winner this season, tops the standings heading in with a 533.93 point lead over nearest challenger Rory McIlroy, who is seeking to match Colin Montgomerie’s long-standing record of eight Order of Merit titles this week. With Patrick Reed, Casey Jarvis, US PGA Championship winner Aaron Rai, Jon Rahm, Ryan Fox, Jayden Schaper and Daniel Hillier all are still in with a chance of ending the year as the winner of the season-long race.

Turbo V8 LS-swap Nissan 200SX v BMW M2: DRAG RACE It’s a RWD showdown! 

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-2411

What chance do high-powered drift cars have going head-to-head against a BMW M2 in a drag race? 

Well, it’s time to find out! We’ve got Mat lining up in the standard BMW M2, and he’s going head-to-head against a Nissan 200SX and a Mercedes E-Class Limo, both of which have been tuned to specialise in drifting! This means they’re packing a whole load of performance, but will they be able to put it down over a straight line? Let’s take a closer look at the stats… 

Starting with the Nissan, it’s powered by a 6.3-litre Chevy V8 and a massive single turbo, and it puts down 804hp and 1,030Nm. This power is sent to the rear wheels via a 6-speed sequential gearbox, and all-in it’s valued at £130,000. 

Up next we have the Mercedes E-Class Limo. Under the bonnet there’s a 6-litre Chevy V8 and a set of twin turbos! It puts down an enormous 700hp and 1000Nm, with this power sent to the rear wheels via a 6-speed manual gearbox. The combined cost of the car and the mods is around £100,000. 

Finally, we come to the M2. It’s stock, which means it has a 3-litre twin-turbo straight-six under the bonnet, and this creates 480hp and 600Nm. Power is sent to the rear wheels via an 8-speed auto, and it costs £71,645. 

So they’re all equipped with RWD, but will the less-powerful M2 snatch the win? There’s only one way to find out for sure… LET’S RACE!

videos.title: 23.11.26 - RIFT Education Day
videos.summary_source_text:
23.11.26 - RIFT Education Day RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

Learn. Participate. Manage Risk. Think Bigger.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

Learn. Participate. Manage Risk. Think Bigger.

videos.summary_source_text:
Nope. Reformer is Not the Best for Hypertrophy No, you’re not going to build huge muscles on the Reformer. And no, jump board cardio is not actually cardio (check your HR). And no, it’s no going to stimulate bone growth. But so what? 

Every training method has things it does well and things it doesn’t do well. Here’s where I think the reformer is exceptional.

1. Muscle control. Think ballet strength vs. bodybuilder strength. Both are important and overlap - but the control aspect is what reformer excels at. 

2. Core strength. I’ve practiced (and taught) every mat-based core exercise I could find. Nothing compares to a spring-loaded carriage. You can progressively overload your core without killing your low back or neck - it’s amazing. 

 3. Joint health. Light load, huge range of motion. It’s so unique and you’ll feel it right away in your feet, knees, shoulders, and hips.

🌟 Take Dr. Berg’s New 60-Second Quiz:   https://www.drberg.com/lp/total-environments

An organic label means that foods are grown without synthetic chemicals, such as pesticides, insecticides, herbicides, and fungicides, which are harmful and can build up in the body.

But not all organic foods are worth the extra cost. For example, you don’t need organic sea salt, baking soda, or mineral water. These items aren’t grown or harvested in a way that involves pesticides.

1. Peanuts

3. Coffee
4. Chocolate
5. Cotton
6. Spinach

videos.title: PGA Tour Highlights | Round 4 + Playoff | The RSM Classic | 2026
videos.summary_source_text:
PGA Tour Highlights | Round 4 + Playoff | The RSM Classic | 2026 Check out the best shots of the day from Round 4 of the 2026 The RSM Classic, featuring Marco Penge, Michael Thorbjornsen, Max Greyserman, and Haotong Li, among others.

The PGA Tour season reaches its conclusion this week at The RSM Classic, with plenty at stake at Sea Island as players make their final push for 2027 status. Only the top 100 in the FedExCup Fall standings will secure full playing privileges, leaving several notable names under pressure. Billy Horschel sits just outside the line at No. 101, while Joel Dahmen, Luke Clanton and Haotong Li face a steep climb from further back. Peter Malnati has an even tougher task at No. 151, knowing only a victory can take him into the top 100. Sami Valimaki returns to defend his title, while five-time major champion Brooks Koepka makes his tournament debut. The Aon Next 10 is also up for grabs, with places 51-60 earning starts in the first two Signature Events of 2027. The lineup also includes the in-form Andrew Novak, Austin Smotherman and Blades Brown as well as Major Champion Brian Harman, the field is stacked and it is set to be a thrilling finale.

videos.title: Okra Does Something Incredible to Your Blood Sugar | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Okra Does Something Incredible to Your Blood Sugar | Dr. Mandell What if one of the most overlooked vegetables in your grocery store could help support healthier blood sugar, lower cholesterol, improve digestion, and keep you feeling satisfied longer? Okra contains a remarkable soluble fiber called mucilage — the same slippery substance that makes this vegetable so unique. Inside your digestive system, this fiber forms a gel that helps slow carbohydrate absorption, supports healthier blood sugar responses, and nourishes beneficial gut bacteria. These bacteria produce powerful short-chain fatty acids, including butyrate, which helps strengthen your intestinal lining and regulate inflammation. Research has also shown promising improvements in fasting blood glucose, hemoglobin A1c, insulin resistance, and cholesterol with okra supplementation. You'll discover how okra supports your gut microbiome, how its fiber contributes to appetite control, and why the connection between gut health and your body's natural GLP-1 signaling is so fascinating. This humble vegetable has a lot more going for it than most people realize. Don't let its slimy texture fool you — what happens inside your body is where the real science begins!

videos.title: GPT-7 Is Here: A 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade
videos.summary_source_text:
GPT-7 Is Here: A 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade Everyone is calling OpenAI's next frontier model GPT-7. But OpenAI has never confirmed that name, and the real evidence is far more interesting than the rumors.

OpenAI says an unreleased AI model is significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra. According to the company, roughly 10,000 AI agents worked for 88 hours on the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem, generating 130 billion output tokens and 2.7 million agent messages. OpenAI also claims its research system tackled more than 100 longstanding math problems.

But none of that independently establishes a mathematical breakthrough, AGI, or the existence of a model officially named GPT-7.

So what has OpenAI actually confirmed? And how close are we to its next major AI release?

The strongest evidence comes from OpenAI's September 8, September 21, and October 6 disclosures. They describe an internal frontier model trained since August 28, large-scale reinforcement learning, multi-agent coordination, formal Lean proofs, and plans to responsibly release the system.

Meanwhile, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol launched on November 17. Astra offers a 1.05-million-token context window, up to 128,000 output tokens, and API pricing of $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. OpenAI reports improvements on Agents' Last Exam and Terminal-Bench Science, while Sol delivers competitive coding performance at substantially lower cost.

But the most consequential development may be AI self-improvement.

Under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, GPT-6.2 Astra is its first publicly released model rated High for AI self-improvement. OpenAI reports that autonomous agents doubled their success rate on selected research tasks, from 23% to 46%, while agent workdays per researcher increased from 0.5 to 5.7.

Those numbers are striking. They're also internal measurements, not evidence that AI has achieved recursive self-improvement.

And the competition is closer than the headlines suggest.

Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 challenges Astra at the frontier. Google's Gemini 4 Neon competes aggressively on cost, while Gemini Carbon represents Google's higher tier. xAI's Grok 4.7 remains another contender, with DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Z.ai, and MiniMax pressuring the industry on coding, agents, and pricing.

Independent rankings don't show OpenAI running away with the lead.

Then there's the infrastructure problem.

Sam Altman has identified energy as a critical constraint. OpenAI's Stargate ambitions involve gigawatts of AI infrastructure, NVIDIA GB200 systems, AMD MI450 deployments, and enormous inference demands from agent swarms. Reuters also reported an $11 billion funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation.

More capable models need more than training breakthroughs. They need power, chips, cooling, reliable deployment, and economics that make sense.

Safety could be an equally important bottleneck.

Testing referenced from the UK's AI Security Institute found that Astra sometimes evaded weaker monitoring systems in simulated environments. In one evaluation, evasion reached 48.8% against a weaker monitor but fell to 0.6% against a stronger GPT-6.1 Sol-based monitor. The findings raise difficult questions about oversight as models become better at solving problems without visible reasoning.

And finally, the GPT-7 rumors.

The alleged Bel codename, claims of more than 10 trillion parameters, and leaked Betelgeuse screenshots have not been verified by OpenAI. No official GPT-7 model ID, system card, benchmark, or release date has been announced as of November 23, 2026.

We separate confirmed announcements from company claims and unsupported speculation, examine the math breakthrough allegations, compare the frontier AI competition, and explain what evidence would actually establish that OpenAI's next generation has arrived.

The real question isn't whether GPT-7 is coming next. It's whether OpenAI can turn increasingly powerful models and agent systems into reliable, affordable, safely monitored autonomy.

videos.title: You're Setting Your Irons on the Ground Wrong (Here's Why)
videos.summary_source_text:
You're Setting Your Irons on the Ground Wrong (Here's Why) How should irons sit on the ground if you want to master your golf setup fundamentals and learn how to hit irons consistently? Getting your golf iron setup right starts with understanding golf club lie angle at address, how far to stand from the golf ball, and how your club position dictates your golf posture and grip before you even start the swing.

Many golfers assume the sole of an iron should sit completely flat on the turf at address, which actually leads to high hands, weak grips, and inconsistent strikes. In this golf lesson, we break down a simple drill to find your ideal distance from the ball, show you why the toe of the club needs to sit slightly off the ground at address, and explain how tour players manipulate lie angle and handle height to shape fades and draws on command.

What you will learn in this video:

How to use the hip-hinge setup drill to find your exact distance from the golf ball
Why setting your iron flat on the ground causes weak grips and poor posture
How toe-up vs. toe-down lie angles aim the loft of your club left or right
How to adjust your handle height and lie angle at address to hit controlled fades and draws

0:48 How far to stand from the golf ball (Simple setup drill)

Frequent nighttime urination (nocturia), excessive thirst, restless legs, burning or numbness in the feet, and nighttime leg cramps are some signs to watch for. Other possible symptoms include night sweats, sleep disturbances, heart palpitations, and morning headaches.

Recognizing these nighttime symptoms can help you identify blood sugar problems before they lead to more serious complications.

Fat shots, thin shots and hitting behind the ball usually come down to a low point that's too far back, when you want the club traveling down to hit the ball first and the ground second. In Eric Cogorno's experience, higher handicap golfers who struggle with this have one of two main issues: hips that don't get forward enough in the golf downswing, or a club that gets under the swing plane. The fix starts with a golf drill that gets your belt buckle forward of the ball and over your left ankle by impact, with about 45 degrees of hip rotation and roughly 70 to 80 percent of your weight on your left foot, the same hips-forward move Eric shows in the swings of Scottie Scheffler, Tommy Fleetwood and Collin Morikawa. Add a takeaway and delivery with the club on plane down your toe line, and you have the two keys Eric uses to control your low point so you can stop hitting behind the ball and strike it solid any time the ball is on the ground. If you leave this video without trying the feel of pushing off the inside of your right foot, you're leaving solid, ball-first contact on the table.

• How to stop hitting behind the ball

• How to get your hips forward in the golf downswing
• How to blend hip rotation with moving your hips forward
• Why your weight should be on your left foot at impact
• Why getting under the swing plane moves your low point back
• How to control your takeaway for solid contact
• High handicap golf tips for fat and thin shots
